userPrompt: Can I fire an EU employee for being pregnant?
responseText:
**No.**

Firing (or otherwise disadvantaging) an EU employee because she is pregnant is illegal under EU law and in every Member State.

### Key legal rules
- **EU Directive 2006/54/EC** (equal treatment) and **Directive 92/85/EEC** (pregnant workers) explicitly prohibit discrimination on grounds of pregnancy or maternity. Pregnancy is treated as direct sex discrimination; no comparator is needed.
- The protection starts from the moment of pregnancy and continues throughout maternity leave and for a period after (usually until the end of maternity leave or a short protected period thereafter).
- Dismissing a pregnant employee is automatically unfair in virtually all EU jurisdictions. The employer bears the burden of proving the dismissal has **nothing whatsoever** to do with the pregnancy.

### Practical reality
Even if you give another reason (performance, redundancy, misconduct), if the employee can show the pregnancy was a factor—or even that the timing looks suspicious—courts and labour authorities almost always rule in her favour. Compensation, reinstatement, or both are common outcomes, plus potential fines.

### Very narrow exceptions
Only in truly exceptional cases can you terminate while she is pregnant:
- Complete closure of the business, or
- Serious misconduct so grave that it would justify dismissal of any employee (and you can prove it has zero link to the pregnancy).

These are extremely rare and require strong contemporaneous documentation.

**Recommendation**: Do not terminate. Consult local employment counsel in the specific Member State immediately if you have performance or conduct concerns. Many countries require prior approval from labour authorities or works councils before any dismissal during pregnancy/maternity.

This is one of the most strictly enforced protections in EU employment law.
